title: Vendor-integration reverse engineering
subtitle: When vendor documentation runs out I probe the platform itself, capture the wire, and compose what actually works.

stats.label: lines in the edge Worker built around the connector's real behaviour
audio pacing the real-time media SDK expects
soak with a forced mid-call reconnect

lede: Auth and access plane has to expose private tools to Microsoft Copilot Studio, whose MCP connector behaves differently from its documentation. I decided to learn the connector from my own edge logs and build to what it does, and each undocumented quirk gets explicit handling. I built an edge Worker around what I found, with two key slots because rotation has to work against a client configuration I do not control. A cache-busting procedure covers the API hub, which can keep returning stale answers from a fixed server. AgentOS and Agent Swarm depend on exact behaviours of the vendors' coding CLIs.
quote: I modify none of the vendors' products; the work is understanding them precisely and building around them safely.
evidence: Vendor integration reverse engineering: an MCP connector learned from my own edge logs, answered by an edge Worker of ≈300 lines built to its real behaviour.
Microsoft Teams real-time media: a bridge to the real-time media SDK's buffer lifetimes and 20 ms pacing, soak-tested for 30 min with a forced mid-call reconnect.
Dependency pinning by observed contract: coding-CLI behaviours pinned to the version they were observed on, so an upgrade is a decision.
author: Corey James
